name: Hanun
overview: Hanun was a male figure in the biblical narrative known primarily as the sixth son of Zalaph. He played a role in the post-exilic community by contributing to the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall, specifically repairing a section as recorded in Nehemiah 3:30. There is no additional tribal or familial information provided about him beyond this.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanun means 'favored' in the original language. This proper name is simply presented without indication that it was given by God. The meaning reflects a positive attribute but no further titles or special designations are noted.
familyAndRelationships: Hanun is explicitly identified as the son of Zalaph in Nehemiah 3:30. Scripture does not provide any other family relationships beyond this filial connection, and no tribe or surname is recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Hanun's significance lies in his participation in the restoration of Jerusalem following the Babylonian exile. By repairing a section of the city's wall, he contributed to the physical and spiritual rebuilding of the community under God's providence. His work symbolizes faithful service in the collective effort to restore God's people and their covenantal city.
